name: Coming to England
notes: Floella Benjamin's dramatised Windrush memoir about emigrating from Trinidad to 1960s London; gentle pacing but emotionally weighty themes of racism and displacement.

name: Best in the World
notes: Guinness World Records clip and guessing-game show inviting viewers to play along with record-breaking feats; general reputation from marketing copy.

name: Wow That's Amazing
notes: Science-trick and gadget show hosted by two young presenters; energetic demonstration format typical of CBBC factual entertainment.

name: Dexter Procter: The 10-Year-Old Doctor
notes: Comedy-drama specials about a 10-year-old paediatrician solving medical mysteries; general reputation from marketing copy, not independently verified.

name: DIY Deadly with Steve Backshall
notes: Steve Backshall's craft/build spin-off of the Deadly strand; calmer studio-based format than the field expeditions.

name: Deadly Dinosaurs with Steve Backshall
notes: Steve Backshall's Deadly-strand spin-off applying the same expedition-style factual format to prehistoric creatures.

name: Deadly Mission Shark
notes: Deadly-strand expedition series focused on sharks; same field-adventure factual format as Deadly 60.

name: Deadly Pole to Pole
notes: Deadly-strand expedition series covering polar wildlife; same field-adventure factual format as Deadly 60.

name: Deadly Predators
notes: Deadly-strand series profiling apex predators; same field-adventure factual format as Deadly 60.

name: Shark Bites
notes: Short-form Steve Backshall factual strand on shark biology, combining field footage with studio 'Shark Lab' demonstrations; brief five-minute episodes keep it calmer than the full Deadly expeditions.

name: Stage Stars
notes: Observational-documentary hybrid following students at a performing arts boarding school, described as blending behind-the-scenes footage with glossy performance segments and social-media-style graphics.

name: Style It Out
notes: Fashion-upcycling competition show where young designers rework preloved clothes to a weekly theme; standard reality-competition energy.

name: Game on Grandparents
notes: Esports competition show where kids coach their grandparents to compete in family-friendly video games; lively studio-competition format.

name: Cooking Buddies
notes: Low-key cooking show where a young host teaches simple recipes to a different friend each episode, in exchange for learning a new skill.

name: Go Get Arty
notes: Family art-challenge show hosted by a real YouTube family with a talking-paintbrush sidekick; craft-focused pacing similar to other CBBC art shows.

name: Meet the McQueens
notes: Comedy-reality series following a vegan teen chef and his family's antics, with a simple recipe segment each episode.

name: Ricky Wilson's Art Jam
notes: Musician Ricky Wilson and celebrity guests discuss art and inspiration in his studio; conversational, low-key format.

name: Clipheads
notes: Kids react to and vote on viral videos from around the world; format built around quick surprise reactions, similar in energy to other clip-reaction shows.

name: Gladiators: Epic Pranks
notes: Gladiators spin-off where the stars prank each other and the public at the live arena; short 15-minute episodes with reality-prank-show energy.

name: Saturday Mash-Up! Live
notes: CBBC's long-running live Saturday morning entertainment magazine show, mixing music, games, celebrity guests and audience interaction at a fast, variety-show pace.

name: Silverpoint
notes: Teen sci-fi mystery about kids at an adventure camp uncovering a buried artefact tied to a decades-old disappearance; moderate pacing typical of CBBC's older-skewing drama slate.

name: Gifted
notes: Superpowered-teens drama adapted from Marilyn Kaye's novels, following Scottish teens discovering and mastering extraordinary abilities while evading a shadowy organisation.

name: Girls of Olympus
notes: Animated tween series about three friends who discover they have the powers of Greek goddesses and must balance monster-battling with school life.

name: Pickle Storm
notes: Sitcom about a fantasy-world family adjusting to life in an ordinary UK town, where the daughter's uncontrollable magic causes chaotic mishaps.

name: Theodosia
notes: Edwardian-set fantasy adventure about a young Egyptologist's daughter who unlocks real magic and must battle ancient forces alongside her friends.

name: Davey & Jonesie's Locker
notes: Teen sci-fi comedy about two best friends whose school locker is a portal to alternate versions of their high school, chased by multiverse enforcers.

name: Mystery Lane
notes: CGI-animated detective series starring a hamster sleuth and her brother solving supernatural mysteries in London; standard animated-adventure pacing.

name: Wizards vs Aliens
notes: Sci-fi/fantasy drama pitting a young wizard against an alien threat; general reputation, comparable in tone to other CBBC teen fantasy dramas.

name: The Demon Headmaster
notes: Fantasy drama about a sinister, mind-controlling headmaster and the children who resist him; general reputation from the long-running franchise.

name: The Sarah Jane Adventures
notes: Doctor Who spin-off following an alien-investigating journalist and her young companions; general reputation, similar tier to other CBBC sci-fi drama.

name: Gormiti: The New Era
notes: Live-action fantasy series where teens master elemental powers to summon warrior spirits and battle an evil lord; action-driven format with frequent elemental effects.

name: Girl Troop vs Aliens
notes: Comedy-adventure about a scout troop who discover their summer camp guests are extra-terrestrials; blends comedy, adventure and sci-fi mystery.

name: A Kind of Spark
notes: Drama about an autistic girl campaigning to memorialise victims of historic witch trials in her town; slower-paced and emotionally serious rather than action-driven.

name: Dragon Ball Super
notes: Continuation of the Dragon Ball franchise's martial-arts battles; same high-intensity fight choreography and pacing as other entries in the series.

name: Beyblade X
notes: Competitive spinning-top battle anime; fast-cut tournament action typical of the franchise.

name: Armorsaurs
notes: Live-action/CG series about teen pilots genetically linked to armoured dinosaur companions defending Earth from an alien invasion; billed as action-packed with strong co-viewing appeal.

name: Total Drama
notes: Reality-show parody where animated teen contestants compete in chaotic challenges; same satirical high-energy format as its Total DramaRama spin-off.

name: Total Drama Presents: The Ridonculous Race
notes: Total Drama spin-off following paired contestants racing around the world; slightly less frantic than the core Total Drama format.

name: Winx Club - The Magic Is Back
notes: Revival of the Winx Club magical-girl franchise; same fairy-battle adventure format and tier as the original series.

name: Dragons: The Nine Realms
notes: How to Train Your Dragon spin-off following a new generation of dragon riders; adventure-driven pacing typical of the franchise.

name: Despicable Me Presents: Minion Madness
notes: Minions short-form spin-off built around slapstick chaos; rapid gag-driven pacing consistent with the franchise's film shorts.

name: Kung Fu Panda: Secrets of the Furious Five
notes: Kung Fu Panda spin-off shorts focused on the Furious Five's backstories; martial-arts action pacing consistent with the film franchise.

name: Monsters vs Aliens: Mutant Pumpkins from Outer Space
notes: Halloween special spin-off of the Monsters vs Aliens film; comedic monster-action format aimed at older kids.

name: Nine Minute Ninja
notes: Short-form ninja-themed action comedy; general reputation, standard energy for the format.

name: Ninja Express
notes: Short-form ninja delivery-themed action comedy; general reputation, standard energy for the format.

name: Counterfeit Cat
notes: Surreal sci-fi comedy about a lazy housecat and an alien disguised in a cat costume getting into dangerous scrapes; standard animated-sitcom energy.

name: Grizzy and the Lemmings
notes: Largely wordless slapstick comedy in the Tom and Jerry tradition, centred on a bear-versus-lemmings rivalry over food.

name: Apple & Onion
notes: Deadpan comedy about two childlike anthropomorphic foods navigating a world of other food characters; gentle, low-key humour from the Amazing World of Gumball creator.

name: Taffy
notes: Slapstick preschool-skewing comedy about a stray raccoon posing as a house cat and the dog trying to expose him; chase-based gag format.

name: Submarine Jim
notes: Underwater adventure comedy about a naive young dolphin steering a submarine on wheels with his friends; standard animated-adventure energy.

name: Monster Loving Maniacs
notes: Comedy about three siblings training as monster hunters who secretly prefer protecting the monsters they're supposed to hunt; blends comedy and adventure with themes of fear and family.

name: OOglies
notes: Stop-motion sketch show where household objects with googly eyes come to life in 30-60 second skits; rapid-fire sketch format makes it far quicker-cut than a standard narrative comedy.

name: Duck and Frog
notes: Dialogue-free slapstick sitcom described as having an 'energetic anarchic sense of humour', following Duck's doomed attempts to hold down a new job each episode.

name: The Deep
notes: CGI adventure series about a family of deep-sea explorers investigating an underwater mystery aboard their advanced submarine.

name: Danny and Mick
notes: Slapstick sitcom about two brothers working at a leisure centre, built around real-life mishap-prone physical comedy performers.

name: Class Dismissed
notes: Sketch comedy series set at a chaotic fictional school, featuring stunts and slapstick set pieces each episode.

name: Little Lunch
notes: Australian mockumentary comedy-drama unfolding entirely during a school snack break; understated, dialogue-driven humour rather than fast physical comedy.

name: Almost Never
notes: Tween comedy-drama sitcom; general reputation, standard energy for the format.

name: All at Sea
notes: Family sitcom; general reputation, not independently verified against pacing data.

name: Andy and the Band
notes: Music-themed sitcom about a kid-led band; general reputation, not independently verified against pacing data.

name: Bro's in Control
notes: Sitcom about siblings left in charge; general reputation, not independently verified against pacing data.

name: Born to Spy
notes: Spy-comedy sitcom; general reputation, not independently verified against pacing data.

name: BMX All Stars
notes: BMX-themed drama; general reputation, not independently verified against pacing data.

name: Home Sweet Rome
notes: Coming-of-age comedy about a teen adjusting to a new stepfamily and city after her dad marries an Italian pop star; standard tween-sitcom pacing.

name: Secret Life of Boys
notes: Sitcom about a girl spending the summer with four boy cousins she's never met; mixes comedy with more emotional, character-driven moments.

name: High Hoops
notes: Basketball-themed school sitcom about a gaffe-prone but talented new player turning around a failing team; standard tween-sitcom energy.

name: iCarly
notes: US tween sitcom about teens running their own web show; general reputation, comparable energy to Sam & Cat.

name: Sam & Cat
notes: US tween sitcom spin-off pairing two mismatched roommates who run a babysitting business; general reputation from the franchise.

name: Wolfblood
notes: Fantasy drama about teenagers who can transform into wolves; general reputation, standard tier for CBBC's older-skewing supernatural dramas.

name: Young Dracula
notes: Comedy-horror sitcom about Dracula's teenage son trying to fit in at a normal school; general reputation from the long-running franchise.

name: What's New Scooby-Doo?
notes: 2002 Scooby-Doo series revival; same mystery-solving gang format and pacing as the wider franchise.

name: Itch
notes: Sci-fi adventure drama about a teenager collecting rare elements that turn out to hold a dangerous secret; general reputation.

name: Jamie Johnson
notes: Football drama following a talented young player's rise; general reputation, standard tier for CBBC sport drama.

name: Jamie Johnson FC
notes: Continuation of the Jamie Johnson football drama franchise; same tier and format as the original.

name: Hank Zipzer
notes: Comedy-drama about a dyslexic boy's school misadventures, based on Henry Winkler's novels; general reputation.

name: Hardball
notes: Football-themed drama series; general reputation, standard tier for CBBC sport drama.

name: The Famous Five
notes: Adaptation of Enid Blyton's classic adventure novels; general reputation, gentle mystery-adventure pacing typical of the source material.

name: Just William
notes: Comedy adaptation of Richmal Crompton's William books about a mischievous schoolboy; general reputation, classic sitcom pacing.

name: Malory Towers
notes: Boarding-school drama adapted from Enid Blyton's novels; general reputation, gentler pacing typical of period boarding-school drama.

name: Hetty Feather
notes: Jacqueline Wilson period drama about a Victorian foundling hospital girl; general reputation, standard tier for CBBC historical drama.

name: The Beaker Girls
notes: Tracy Beaker franchise spin-off following Tracy's daughter; family sitcom-drama pacing consistent with the wider franchise.

name: Grandpa's Great Escape
notes: David Walliams TV film about a boy and his grandfather, who has dementia and imagines himself as a WWII Spitfire pilot; more emotionally serious than fast-paced.

name: Gangsta Granny
notes: David Walliams TV film about a boy who discovers his 'boring' grandma was once a jewel thief; comedy-heist family film pacing.

name: Gangsta Granny Strikes Again
notes: Sequel to the Gangsta Granny TV film; same comedy-heist family pacing as the original.

name: Billionaire Boy
notes: David Walliams TV film about a lonely boy whose father won the lottery; comedy pacing typical of the Walliams adaptation strand.

name: Mr Stink
notes: David Walliams TV film about a girl who befriends a homeless man; gentler, more emotionally driven pacing than the comedy-heist entries in the strand.

name: Matilda and the Ramsay Bunch
notes: Reality-comedy series following chef Gordon Ramsay's youngest daughter and her family; general reputation.

name: Millie Inbetween
notes: Comedy-drama about a girl navigating her parents' separation and two households; more emotionally grounded than fast-paced.

name: Princess Mirror-Belle
notes: Fantasy sitcom about a girl whose mirror-world princess double keeps swapping places with her; general reputation.

name: Raven
notes: Fantasy-themed adventure game show where contestants complete physical and mental challenges to defeat a shape-shifting villain; general reputation.

name: 4 O'Clock Club
notes: Musical comedy-drama sitcom about a group of friends forming a dance/music collective; general reputation.

name: 500 Words
notes: BBC Radio 2's short-story-writing competition strand for kids, covered with author interviews and finalist readings; calm, literary-focused format.

name: Absolute Genius with Dick and Dom
notes: Science-history comedy duo demonstrating famous inventions and experiments; energetic double-act presenting style.

name: Britain's Best Young Artist
notes: Art competition series showcasing young artists' work; general reputation, calmer than a typical reality competition.

name: Jennie's Fitness in 5
notes: Short comedic exercise segments where an aerobics instructor's routine keeps getting derailed by chaos and interruptions; energetic but brief format.

name: Lifebabble
notes: Short advice strand tackling awkward and serious issues for kids, from bullying to family relationships; calm, honest, low-key delivery.

name: Own It
notes: BBC's online-safety education initiative for kids, covering privacy, cyberbullying and digital wellbeing through calm advice-led content.

name: Gangnam Project: A K-pop Story
notes: Coming-of-age drama about a Canadian-Korean teen training at an elite K-pop school; musical performance sequences add energy to an otherwise standard drama pace.

name: The Dengineers
notes: Makeover show where a team builds elaborate themed dens for children, ending in a big reveal; excitement is concentrated in reveal moments rather than constant high energy.

name: Boy Girl Dog Cat Mouse Cheese
notes: Animated sitcom about a 'dysfunctional family' whose members are literally a boy, girl, dog, cat, mouse and cheese living together; standard animated-sitcom energy.

name: Dodger
notes: Oliver Twist prequel-style drama following the Artful Dodger and Fagin's gang through Victorian London's criminal underworld; more serious period drama than fast-paced adventure.

name: Gym Stars
notes: Behind-the-scenes documentary following young UK gymnasts training across artistic, trampoline and acrobatic disciplines; observational factual pacing.

name: Katy
notes: Jacqueline Wilson drama about a strong-willed girl adjusting to life with a spinal cord injury after an accident; emotionally serious themes of disability and identity outweigh any fast pacing.

name: Lagging
notes: Comedy-drama following a group of five 12-year-old gamers navigating friendship and real life alongside their online gaming sessions.

name: Muddle Earth
notes: Animated Lord of the Rings parody about a boy summoned to a medieval fantasy world to stand in for a bumbling wizard against a villain; comic fantasy-adventure pacing.

name: My Mum Tracy Beaker
notes: Tracy Beaker franchise continuation following Tracy as an adult raising her own daughter; family drama pacing, more grounded than the earlier care-home instalments.

name: Mystic
notes: Environmental teen drama about a girl who moves to New Zealand and befriends the town's horse riders while fighting an industrial development threatening their coastline.

name: Nova Jones
notes: Comedy-adventure about a teen pop star touring the galaxy with her family and bandmates, featuring original songs each series; musical-performance energy alongside sitcom-style family conflict.

name: Potato Party
notes: One-minute animated shorts following a group of potato characters through comedic mini-adventures; brief rapid-fire episode format similar to other short-form sketch comedies.

name: Sherwood (Animated)
notes: Animated Robin Hood adaptation following the outlaw and his band in Sherwood Forest; standard adventure-comedy pacing for the format.

name: Show Me the Honey!
notes: Beekeeping competition show where kids learn apiary skills and compete to produce the tastiest honey; calmer, nature-focused format compared to typical CBBC competition shows.

name: So Awkward
notes: Mockumentary-style sitcom following a group of teen friends through everyday embarrassing moments; general reputation, standard tween-sitcom energy.

name: Spooky Files
notes: Live-action comedy about a crew of kids capturing supernatural 'Spookies' appearing around their town, blending retro 80s/90s nostalgia with mystery and just-right scares.

name: Super Happy Magic Forest
notes: Animated fantasy-comedy adaptation of Matty Long's books, following five forest heroes who battle villains while mostly just wanting to picnic and frolic together.

name: The Adventures of Mansour: Age of AI
notes: Animated action-adventure about a tech-whiz boy who accidentally creates a mischievous rogue AI and must team up with friends to contain the chaos it causes.

name: The Boy in the Dress
notes: David Walliams TV film about a boy who discovers a love of fashion and wearing dresses; gentler, more emotionally driven pacing focused on acceptance and bullying themes.

name: The Football Academy
notes: Documentary following young players at professional football academies as they chase a career in the sport, balancing training pressure with school and personal challenges.

name: The Lady Grace Mysteries
notes: Tudor-court mystery drama about a lady-in-waiting secretly working as the Queen's teenage spy, solving plots and mysteries amid palace intrigue.

name: The Next Step
notes: Canadian dance-drama following a competitive dance studio's students; general reputation, standard tier for CBBC's dance/music drama slate.

name: The Story of Tracy Beaker
notes: Original Jacqueline Wilson drama about a spirited girl in a children's care home; general reputation, standard tier for the franchise.

name: The Strange Chores
notes: Animated series about two teens and a ghost girl learning to take over an ageing monster-slayer's supernatural chores; action-comedy pacing from the Bluey co-creators' other project.

name: Tracy Beaker Returns
notes: Sequel series to The Story of Tracy Beaker, following Tracy back at the care home as a volunteer; general reputation, standard tier for the franchise.

name: Danny Go
notes: High-intensity 'brain break' movement and dance videos designed for kids to get up and move rather than sit passively, similar in format and energy to GoNoodle. General reputation from parent/teacher guides, not independently verified against pacing data.

name: MrBeast
notes: Common Sense Media rates the main channel 14+ due to risky stunts, heavy product promotion, and how money and fame are presented, and notes the 'fast-paced editing and constant energy can overstimulate' — but flags it's widely watched by much younger kids despite that guidance.

name: Mark Rober
notes: Common Sense Media describes the videos as 'fast-paced with lots of interesting images and helpful graphics' built around 'extreme experiments' and 'sensationalized stunts'; also flags that CrunchLabs product promos are woven directly into videos without a clear break, making them hard for kids to distinguish from the content.

name: Yo Gabba GabbaLand!
notes: 2024 Apple TV+ reboot of the neon, music-and-dance format; reviews warn colors 'can flash quickly' and the show 'could be overstimulating,' with rapid transitions and dense songs, though content is emotionally gentle.

name: StarBeam
notes: Reviews describe a vibrant but soft palette made for 'little eyes,' comical (non-scary) villains, and simple one-or-two-step plots; StarBeam even models taking a breath before acting, keeping intensity moderate.

name: The Creature Cases
notes: Parents repeatedly call it 'overwhelming due to its high stimulation and fast-paced scenes,' with fast dialogue and 'unexpected twists that keep kids on the edge of their seats,' though it is non-violent and educational.

name: Kid-E-Cats
notes: Short (~4-5 min) wholesome kitten adventures; reviewers describe a 'calm pace with nice and charming characters' suited to low-key background viewing. General reputation from reviews, not independently verified against measured pacing data.

name: Rhyme Time Town
notes: Described as 'visually stimulating without overwhelming sensory input' and 'a calm viewing option... suitable for wind-down periods'; song-driven and warm, but noted as highly repetitive in songs and storylines.

name: Team Zenko Go
notes: Parents flag that the 'pacing is weirdly fast and intense for such gentle content' with 'intense music, which could be overstimulating for some toddlers,' despite no violence or scary material.

name: Monkie Kid
notes: Common Sense Media calls it 'fast-moving, suspenseful, and frenetic,' packing full arcs into ~10 minutes with 'lots of cartoon violence' and 'scary, loud villains' — the most action-intense of this batch.

name: Ni Hao, Kai-Lan
notes: Built on a 'think-along, play-along' format with planned pauses for viewer responses, making it inherently slow; teaches gentle handling of feelings like fear and jealousy. Rated from general knowledge of this established Dora-style show.

name: Get Rolling with Otis
notes: Common Sense Media calls it a 'gentle, slow-paced show... perfect for very young kids' with calm, colorful (not garish) animation and simple stories built around naming feelings — the quietest entry in this batch.

name: Barney & Friends
notes: Slow, soft-spoken pacing and reassuring emotional tone, but the screen is filled with bright colors and near-constant upbeat sing-along numbers, giving it an elevated sensory load despite its gentle rhythm.

name: Gigantosaurus
notes: CGI preschool dino-adventure with recurring musical frolic sequences and bright, saturated visuals; reviews (Forbes, Common Sense) describe teamwork-driven stories with moderate action energy rather than frantic pacing. Cut speed and pacing estimated from general viewing, not scene-timed.

name: Ben 10 (2016)
notes: Reboot reviews note the 'bad guys come fast and furious' with a bright palette, rapid alien transformations, and comedy-forward but high-energy action; loud, dense sensory load. High-end factors inferred from reviews, not independently scene-timed.

name: The Smurfs (2021)
notes: Common Sense Media's review states this reboot has 'more action, more perilous moments, and less character build-up than the original,' citing chases, cliff falls, and exploding potions - a moderate step up in emotional spikes and pace from the 1980s series.

name: Trotro
notes: Repeatedly listed among low-stimulation toddler shows: gentle, slow, natural-language storytelling built around everyday routines of a little donkey, with calm visuals and quiet audio. Rated from those descriptions, not scene-timed.

name: Do, Re & Mi
notes: Song-driven preschool series (KidsFirst/Common Sense) that explicitly teaches music concepts like tempo and dynamics; multiple songs per episode add sensory density but the overall rhythm is gentle and unhurried. Rated from reviews, not independently verified.

name: Sooty (2011)
notes: Live puppet slapstick built around water pranks, magic mishaps and 'playful chaos' per series descriptions; single-set staging keeps cuts moderate while the comic set-pieces give it a livelier tempo. Rated from reviews, not scene-timed.

name: Rev & Roll
notes: Common Sense Media describes it as 'a calm show ideal for young preschoolers not ready for TV with too much conflict,' with no scary content or perilous situations despite its vehicle-adventure premise - keeping emotional and pace scores low.

name: Pop Paper City
notes: Vibrant paper-world preschool show that alternates gentle 3D adventures with live-action craft montages encouraging kids to make their own creations; colorful but low-conflict and unhurried. Rated from descriptions, pacing not independently verified.

name: Trolls: TrollsTopia
notes: Common Sense Media highlights 'great music' and 'lots of random silliness,' with catchy numbers in constantly changing musical styles and a bright, glittery, high-energy palette - a loud, dense, fast-feeling show. Cut-speed and pacing inferred from reviews, not scene-timed.

name: The InBESTigators
notes: Dialogue-driven Aussie mockumentary ('an Office for kids') where kid detectives solve low-stakes mysteries; talking-head format and gentle humor keep cuts, sensory load and emotional spikes modest. Rated from reviews, not scene-timed.
